name: the hand-passed card as a physical object
function: It is small enough to go in a pocket, made in a run, and it moves by one person giving it to another. Nobody encounters it on a wall and nobody finds it by looking; it arrives because somebody decided to hand it over, and that decision is part of the work's distribution. The person who receives it either keeps it or throws it away within the day, and most throw it away.
consequences: It is read at reading distance, held, by one person at a time, with no far reading at all. Everything happens in the hand and nothing has to survive being seen across a room.

It arrives through a social act. Somebody had to be willing to give it, which means it has to be a thing a person is not embarrassed to hand over, and the giver's willingness is a harder constraint than the receiver's attention.
It is small, so surface is the scarcest thing there is. What is included is included at the cost of something else, and there is no room at all for a second thought.

It is one of many identical objects, most of which are discarded. The run is large, the survival rate is low, and the object has to be worth keeping for a reason the receiver can articulate to themselves in about four seconds.

It is incomplete on its own. A thing this size cannot carry a whole account of anything, so it either points somewhere else or it is a fragment of a set the receiver does not have, and both of those are decisions rather than accidents.
It survives in pockets, wallets, books and drawers, which means creasing, softening at the corners, and being found again a year later by somebody who has forgotten where it came from.
It is cheap per unit and produced in quantity, so the process is a short-run one with flat inks on light stock, and the material itself signals disposability whatever is on it.
It can be passed on again. Unlike anything fixed to a surface, it has a second and third owner, and what it says has to still work when the person handing it over is a stranger rather than the maker.
doesNotDecide: Composition, palette, imagery, type, tone, what is on the reverse, whether it points elsewhere or stands alone, how much of the surface is used, and what the piece is about. None of that follows from the object being small and given away.
